title: Are you a slave?
html:
I have been reading an interesting book called ‘Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance’ by Robert Pirsig. In it, he talks about a slave mentality which has been built into people by years of carrot and whip grading, and a mule mentality which says, "If you don't whip me, I won't work."

So you don't get whipped and you don't work. This made me think about the phrase, ‘kick up the behind’, that is always said to people who aren't working hard, in the hopes of getting them to work harder.

Why do people need a kick up the butt to do what they know they should do? I have had a fair few verbal kicks over the years and I have wondered why I would need one. I am not lazy and my cup runs over in the enthusiasm department.

Then an "Aha!" moment… I sometimes need a kick up the behind when I am veering off course or taking on too much. Why? Because life becomes like an old TV on the fritz, horizontal lines running across it, and it needs a whack to get the picture back in focus.

Is that you? Do you sometimes need a whack to get back into focus? I have noticed the people who do this for me have my best interests in mind, have been through what I am going through and want to stop me from having to suffer. ‘Whacked with love’, you might say.

Have a terrific week and have a think about whether you're being a slave or not.
